entries.stat: GoFundMe acquired Classy in January 2022 for $484 million
Donorbox has processed over $2 billion in donations for 50,000+ nonprofits globally as of 2024
Nonprofits using donation-form-only tools as their primary CRM report spending 3-5 hours per week on manual reconciliation between donation records and grant tracking spreadsheets
Bonterra's 2022 merger combined EveryAction, Network for Good, Apricot, and other nonprofit software products under one umbrella
Funraise was founded in 2016 and serves thousands of nonprofits with fundraising form and campaign tools
60%+ of mid-sized nonprofits using fundraising-first platforms report needing a secondary system for donor relationship management
Bloomerang acquired Kindful in June 2021 for an undisclosed sum
The nonprofit CRM market sees 40%+ of organizations considering platform changes within any 24-month window
Mid-sized nonprofits ($500K-$10M budget) managing 3+ active grants typically require separate grant tracking tools when using donor-only CRMs, adding $100-$400/month in supplementary software cost
Neon One has made at least five acquisitions in the nonprofit software space including Arts People, Rallybound, and others
Salesforce-based nonprofit implementations (NPSP, Nimble AMS) have typical year-one consulting costs of $15,000-$75,000 based on nonprofit technology survey data
Bloomerang acquired Qgiv in 2024, integrating Qgiv's peer-to-peer and event fundraising tools into the Bloomerang ecosystem
Organizations using fundraising-form-only platforms alongside a separate CRM report managing two separate donor records systems in over 60% of cases
Illinois has approximately 73,000 registered 501(c)(3) public charities, with the Chicago metro accounting for approximately 30,000 - roughly 41% of the state total
Illinois Attorney General Charitable Trust Bureau registers approximately 23,000 charitable organizations under the Illinois Solicitation for Charity Act, requiring AG-440 annual filings

MacArthur Foundation distributed approximately $290 million in grants in 2023; Joyce Foundation distributed approximately $50 million in 2023; together they fund a meaningful share of Chicago-area institutional grant dollars
Illinois requires an independent audit attached to AG-990 filings for charitable organizations with gross contributions over $300,000, a notably lower threshold than New York's $1 million
Chicago metro nonprofits collectively employ approximately 350,000-400,000 workers across health care, social services, education, and arts subsectors
Sector-wide donor retention in Chicago tracks national AFP Fundraising Effectiveness Project data at 43-46%, with first-year retention at 19-23% and multi-year retention at 60-65%
The sector-wide nonprofit donor retention rate was 43.6% in 2023, meaning 56.4% of donors who gave in 2022 did not make another gift in 2023
First-year (new) donor retention averages 19-23% - fewer than one in four new donors makes a second gift
Multi-year (repeat) donor retention averages 60-65%, meaning organizations that cultivate donors through the second gift retain nearly two-thirds in subsequent years
The average cost to acquire a new donor is $25-$50, compared to $4-$8 to retain an existing donor - a 5:1 to 12:1 cost differential
A 10-percentage-point improvement in retention rate - from 43% to 53% - increases a nonprofit's five-year cumulative revenue by approximately 25-30%, holding acquisition constant
Allowable costs/cost principles findings account for 28% of all compliance findings in nonprofit Single Audits, making it the most frequently cited finding category for five consecutive fiscal years
43% of compliance findings in nonprofit Single Audits are repeat findings - findings that were identified in a prior audit period and have not been fully resolved
The average disallowance amount for an allowable costs finding at a nonprofit organization is $23,000-$67,000 per finding, depending on award size and the scope of the violation

68% of nonprofits that receive a compliance finding in their first Single Audit have no dedicated grant compliance staff - grant management is handled by the executive director, a program director, or a development associate

Organizations using dedicated grants management software have a 22-percentage-point lower compliance finding rate than organizations tracking grants in spreadsheets, controlling for organization size and grant portfolio complexity
Government grants and contracts represent 65% of total grant revenue for human services nonprofits, compared to 38% for arts and culture organizations
The average time from federal grant application submission to award notification is 4.2 months for competitive discretionary grants
Renewal win rates for existing government grantees average 68-75% across major federal agencies including HHS, DOJ, and HUD
New grant win rates from private foundations average 20-25% for unsolicited proposals and 35-45% for invited proposals
Texas has approximately 117,000 registered 501(c)(3) public charities, with the Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land MSA accounting for approximately 15,000 - roughly 13% of the state total

Houston Endowment, founded by Jesse H. Jones and Mary Gibbs Jones, has approximately $2.7 billion in assets and distributes approximately $90-100 million in grants annually, making it one of the largest single-region private foundations in the United States

Texas does not require state-level charitable solicitation registration for most 501(c)(3) public charities, in contrast to New York, Illinois, and California; Texas charities file a state Public Information Report (PIR) with the Texas Comptroller and otherwise rely on federal Form 990 for state-level oversight
United Way of Greater Houston raised approximately $80-90 million in its most recent campaign, distributing funds to a network of approximately 80-100 partner agencies across the Houston region

Hurricane Harvey (2017) drove approximately $1.6 billion in philanthropic disaster-relief giving to Houston-area nonprofits within 12 months of landfall, the largest single-event philanthropic mobilization in Texas history
Sector-wide donor retention in Houston tracks national AFP Fundraising Effectiveness Project data at 43-46%, with first-year retention at 19-23% and multi-year retention at 60-65%
California has approximately 195,000 registered 501(c)(3) public charities, with Los Angeles County accounting for approximately 30,000 - the largest single-county concentration in the state

LA County's Measure H quarter-cent sales tax for homelessness services generates approximately $355 million annually, the largest dedicated local revenue stream for homelessness services in the country

California requires Form RRF-1 annual filings from charitable organizations registered with the Registry of Charitable Trusts; the audit threshold is gross revenue of $2 million or more for an attached audit
LA County nonprofits collectively employ approximately 350,000-400,000 workers, with health care and social services representing the largest single employment subsector
Sector-wide donor retention in LA tracks national AFP Fundraising Effectiveness Project data at 43-46%, with first-year retention at 19-23% and multi-year retention at 60-65%
The California Community Foundation distributed approximately $250 million in grants in 2023; the Annenberg Foundation distributed approximately $90 million in 2023 from its LA-area programs
56% of nonprofits with revenues under $1 million use QuickBooks as their primary accounting system, compared to 22% using a purpose-built nonprofit accounting platform
The median annual cost of purpose-built nonprofit accounting software (fund accounting with grant tracking) is $4,800-$12,000 for organizations with $500K-$5M budgets
Organizations using purpose-built fund accounting software spend an average of 6.2 hours per week less on manual reconciliation than those using adapted small-business software
The average cost to remediate a Single Audit material weakness is $18,000-$42,000 in staff time, audit fees, and corrective action plan implementation

Only 34% of nonprofits subject to Single Audit (federal expenditures exceeding $1,000,000) have an accounting system capable of producing a Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (SEFA) without manual spreadsheet construction

Approximately 32,000 nonprofit organizations filed Single Audit reports with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse in fiscal year 2022, representing organizations with federal expenditures exceeding $1,000,000
34.8% of Single Audits filed by nonprofit organizations in FY2022 contained at least one finding - either a material weakness, significant deficiency, or compliance finding

The five most frequent finding categories in nonprofit Single Audits are: allowable costs/cost principles (28% of findings), activities allowed/unallowed (19%), reporting (17%), cash management (14%), and subrecipient monitoring (11%)
48% of nonprofits that receive a material weakness finding in year one receive a repeat finding in year two, compared to 23% for significant deficiencies
The average cost to resolve a material weakness - including corrective action plan development, incremental audit fees, and system or process changes - is $18,000-$42,000
62% of nonprofits with annual revenues above $500,000 report using a dedicated CRM for donor management; the rate drops to 31% for organizations under $250,000 in revenue
Data quality is cited as a top-3 technology challenge by 71% of nonprofits that use a CRM - the most frequently cited challenge for the fifth consecutive year
Only 24% of nonprofits that use a CRM report using it for grant tracking - the majority track grants in spreadsheets, even when a CRM is in use for donor management
Overall CRM satisfaction in the nonprofit sector averages 3.4 out of 5.0 - below the 3.8 average satisfaction reported for accounting software in the same survey
The average cost of CRM implementation - including licensing, configuration, data migration, and training - is $8,000-$22,000 for nonprofits with donor files of 1,000-10,000 records
52% of nonprofits surveyed reported having 3 months or fewer of operating reserves in 2024
36% of nonprofits ended FY2024 operating at a structural deficit - spending more than they earned for the year
Nonprofits with $1M-$5M budgets held a median of 47 days cash on hand in 2023, compared to 91 days for organizations with budgets above $10M
Only 32% of nonprofits reported having a formal operating reserve policy in 2024
The median management and general expense ratio for nonprofits with $1M-$5M budgets was 18.3% of total expenses in FY2023
Nonprofits with M&G ratios below 12% are 2.3x more likely to have a material audit finding related to financial controls in their most recent audit
Only 22% of nonprofits that qualify for a negotiated indirect cost rate under 2 CFR 200.414 have actually negotiated one - leaving federal cost recovery on the table
The de minimis indirect cost rate under 2 CFR 200.414(b) is 10% of modified total direct costs (MTDC) - available to any organization that has never had a negotiated rate
New York State has approximately 95,000 registered 501(c)(3) public charities, with roughly 40,000 headquartered in New York City according to IRS Business Master File and NCCS data
The New York State Charities Bureau registers approximately 87,000 charitable organizations under Article 7-A of the Executive Law, the broadest single-state registry in the country
NYC nonprofits collectively report over $200 billion in annual revenue and employ approximately 600,000 workers, making the nonprofit sector roughly 15% of total NYC private-sector employment
Government contracts and grants account for approximately 60% of NYC nonprofit revenue across the human services subsector, with city contracts alone exceeding $7 billion annually
Approximately 11% of NY State registered charities meet the CHAR500 audit threshold (gross revenue over $1 million in NY State), requiring an independent audit attached to the annual filing
Sector-wide donor retention in NYC tracks national AFP Fundraising Effectiveness Project data at 43-46%, with first-year retention at 19-23% and multi-year retention at 60-65%

The District of Columbia and adjacent jurisdictions (Northern Virginia, Suburban Maryland) collectively host approximately 10,000 registered 501(c)(3) public charities, the highest per-capita nonprofit density of any US metro

Federal pass-through grants and direct federal contracts can account for 60-70% of revenue across the DC metro human services and policy subsectors, the highest federal-dependency rate of any US metro nonprofit sector

The Combined Federal Campaign (CFC), the federal employee workplace giving program, raised approximately $80 million in its most recent annual campaign across all CFC zones nationally, with the National Capital Area zone the largest single contributor
Washington DC has approximately 5,500 nonprofits headquartered in the District alone, plus an estimated 2,500 in Northern Virginia and 2,000 in Suburban Maryland in the adjacent counties

DC requires charitable solicitation registration through the DC Office of the Attorney General; Virginia requires registration through the Office of Charitable and Regulatory Programs (OCRP); Maryland requires registration through the Secretary of State Charities Division
Sector-wide donor retention in DC tracks national AFP Fundraising Effectiveness Project data at 43-46%, with first-year retention at 19-23% and multi-year retention at 60-65%
Blackbaud has reported 45,000+ customers across its product portfolio in recent annual filings, with Raiser's Edge family products serving a substantial share of US fundraising organizations.

Blackbaud's 2020 ransomware incident - disclosed publicly - affected hundreds of nonprofit, education, and healthcare customers and remains relevant context for procurement and data-handling decisions on the platform.

Nonprofit Quarterly and Idealware industry surveys consistently report ERP implementation budgets exceeding $100,000 for organizations adopting NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or comparable enterprise platforms.
Sage Intacct is the AICPA's preferred provider of financial management software, a partnership in place since 2017.

Industry data from Idealware and TechSoup consistently reports nonprofit CRM migration projects run 6-16 weeks for mid-sized organizations and produce 5-15% recurring donor attrition through transition without proactive communication.
The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta distributed over $200 million in grants in 2023 across competitive, designated, donor-advised, and field-of-interest funds
Robert W. Woodruff Foundation has awarded over $4 billion in grants since its founding, with a current annual giving rate of approximately $200 million
Georgia has approximately 47,000 registered nonprofits, with roughly 60% in the Atlanta metro statistical area
Greater Boston has approximately 1,800 private foundations registered with the Massachusetts Attorney General's Non-Profit Organizations/Public Charities Division
The Boston Foundation distributed approximately $200 million in grants in FY2023 from its combined discretionary and donor-advised fund pools
Cummings Foundation has awarded over $500 million in grants to Massachusetts nonprofits since its founding in 1986, with the annual $30K and $100K open program directing roughly $30 million per year
Daniels Fund has awarded over $1.7 billion in grants and scholarships since 2000 across its four-state region (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, Wyoming)
The Denver Foundation distributed over $130 million in grants in 2023 across its community grants and donor-advised fund pools
Colorado has approximately 26,000 registered nonprofits, with roughly 60% headquartered in the Denver metro and Front Range corridor
McKnight Foundation distributed approximately $130 million in grants in 2023 across its arts, environment, education, and Mississippi River programs
Bush Foundation has awarded over $1 billion in grants since its founding in 1953, with current annual grantmaking of approximately $50 million
Minnesota has approximately 31,000 registered nonprofits, with roughly half headquartered in the Twin Cities seven-county metro
Seattle Foundation distributed over $235 million in grants in 2023 across its discretionary, donor-advised, and designated fund pools
Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has awarded over $77.6 billion in grants since inception, the largest cumulative grantmaking total of any private foundation in the United States
Washington State has approximately 36,000 registered nonprofits, with the Puget Sound region accounting for over half
